title: Koreans Heat the Floor, Not the Air

slides.headline: Koreans don't heat the air. **They heat the floor.**
slides.note: And they've done it for centuries.

slides.headline: It's called **ondol**
slides.body: Ondol (온돌) means "warm stone". Heat runs under the floor, so the whole room warms from the ground up.

slides.headline: Once fire, **now hot water**
slides.body: Old houses sent kitchen fire smoke through stone channels under the floor. Today, pipes carry hot water from a boiler instead.

slides.headline: The warmest spot **goes to elders**
slides.body: The floor nearest the fire was the hottest. That spot, araetmok (아랫목), was saved for grandparents and guests.

slides.headline: Life happens **on the floor**
slides.body: Koreans sit, eat and sleep on the floor. A warm floor turns the whole room into a seat and a bed.

slides.headline: That's why **shoes come off**
slides.body: You don't walk on a bed in shoes. Same logic for a floor you lie on every night.

slides.headline: Hot air rises. **Warm floors don't.**
slides.body: Heaters and radiators warm your head first. Ondol warms your feet first, and the heat stays low where you live.

slides.headline: The year heating became **heritage**
slides.body: Korea named ondol culture a National Intangible Cultural Heritage in 2018.

slides.headline: Not just heating. **A way of living.**
slides.body: In Korea, home starts at the floor, and the floor is warm.

slides.headline: Korea, explained **by a Korean.**
slides.body: Follow for the context behind the things Korea does.
slides.graphic: Seoul apartment blocks at dusk with warm window lights, softly blurred behind the text.

caption:
Korean homes don't heat the air. They heat the floor, a system called ondol that Koreans have lived on for centuries.

It's why Koreans sit, eat and sleep on the floor, and why shoes always come off at the door.

Where does the heat come from in your home?
reply: One more: many Koreans who sleep in a bed still put an electric heating mat (전기장판) under the sheets in winter. The warm-floor habit follows them even off the floor. How do people in your country keep warm at night when it gets cold?
fact_check: 1장 note: '수백 년'으로 보수적으로 씀. 고고학상 기원은 기원전까지 거슬러 올라간다는 설명이 일반적.
2장: 온돌(溫突)=따뜻하게 데운 돌/구들. 'warm stone' 의역.
3장: 아궁이 불의 열·연기가 구들 고래를 지나 굴뚝으로. 현대 아파트는 온수 배관 바닥난방.
4장: 아랫목=아궁이 가까운 가장 따뜻한 자리, 어른·손님 자리. 일반적 설명.
8장: 온돌문화, 2018-04-30 국가무형문화재 지정 확인(세계일보·경향 2018). 2,000년 이상 역사로 소개됨.
댓글: 전기장판 사용. 일반적 생활상, 통계 없음.
